significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that numerical magnitude has a form-invariant geometry across digits and number words and that arithmetic consumes this shared representation "before language-specific verbalization"—a form-(iii) invariance and computational-ordering claim, strengthened by the causal assertion that disrupting it impairs arithmetic across languages. This would establish both a sharply bounded phenomenon (cross-form numerical equivalence) and a mechanism, fixing expectations about where lexical forms converge and separating shared calculation from output rendering; this matters to the latent-language question studied by Wendler et al., “Do Llamas Work in English?” (ACL 2024), and to geometric accounts such as Engels et al., “Not All Language Model Features Are Linear: The Case of Numerical Addition” (2024). The branches are determinate: failure of invariant geometry or language-general causal effects would rule out the proposed universal shared-code pipeline, although it would not by itself select among multiple language-specific alternatives. Topic-substitution check: the broad multilingual-representation topic alone would not earn this score; the claim-specific invariance across lexical forms plus the ordering of shared arithmetic before verbalization makes it stronger than the median shared-subspace hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed "shared magnitude subspace," its "form-invariant magnitude manifold," and a magnitude probe whose interpretation is numerical quantity; the probe is mainly a post-hoc diagnostic, while subspace intervention is a control knob rather than an ex-ante failure forecast. After per-model re-extraction, the conclusion predicts a substantive relation—cross-form geometric invariance and language-uniform arithmetic dependence—rather than merely supplying a procedure for searching, so recalibration would not erase its main content. The hypothesis is phrased broadly over multilingual models and lexicalizations, but it does not explicitly guarantee transfer across architectures, scales, training regimes, or quantities beyond the acknowledged small-number regime; likely downstream users are multilingual-model and interpretability researchers, with a possible but unstated model-auditing use. Topic-substitution check: multilingual transfer alone would not justify this score; the named quantitative manifold and its predicted cross-language causal role provide the claim-specific reach, satisfying relation-that-transfers but not clear lead time or established uptake outside the research community.
